verdict: General Mills' sales fell 3% to $4.4B after it sold its U.S. yogurt business, and EPS dropped to $0.74 — mostly because last year's quarter contained a $1.0B gain on that very sale.

segments.name: North America Retail
segments.note: Cereals, meals, snacks and baking in U.S. and Canadian stores — down 7%, including a 4-point drag from selling the U.S. yogurt business.

segments.name: International
segments.note: Sales outside North America — the only segment that grew solidly.

segments.name: North America Pet
segments.note: Blue Buffalo pet food — flat year over year.

segments.note: Sales to restaurants, schools and other foodservice customers.

segments.note: Small corporate and other sales that are not part of a segment.

opex.note: Selling, general and administrative costs across the food brands.

opex.note: Restructuring, transformation, impairment and other exit costs.

otherDetail: Interest, net of $142.2M, partly offset by $10.6M of benefit-plan non-service income and $18.9M of after-tax earnings from joint ventures (mainly Cereal Partners Worldwide and Häagen-Dazs Japan) — the chart's other line is the net -$112.7M.
footerNote: Net earnings in the chart total $398.1M including noncontrolling interests; $397.0M was attributable to General Mills. Joint-venture earnings are reported after tax, below the tax line, as General Mills presents them.

takeaways.title: Last year's gain haunts the comparison
takeaways.text: A year ago General Mills booked a $1,054M gain on the U.S. yogurt divestiture. Without it, operating profit fell 11% in constant currency (adjusted) rather than the reported 63% — still a decline, driven by the lost yogurt sales.

takeaways.title: Organic sales were flat
takeaways.text: Organic net sales were flat: volume fell 4 points and price/mix added 1 point (with a divestiture drag on reported volume). North America Retail fell 7% reported; International grew 4%.

takeaways.title: Guidance held
takeaways.text: Adjusted EPS of $0.75 fell 13% in constant currency, and the company reaffirmed its full-year fiscal 2027 outlook — betting on new products and brand investment to restart growth.

oneTimers: The year-ago quarter included a $1,054.4M gain on the divestiture of the U.S. yogurt business; this quarter has no divestiture gain, which explains most of the reported profit decline.
Restructuring, transformation, impairment and other exit costs were $21.4M in the quarter.
